title_en: Duan Tianguo v. People's Insurance Company of China, Nanjing Branch — dispute over insurance contract

full_text_en:
Duan Tianguo v. PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited, Nanjing Branch — dispute over an insurance contract

Ruling Summary

In accordance with Article 17, paragraph 1, and Article 18 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, as amended in 2002, when concluding an insurance contract, the insurer shall explain the terms and contents of the insurance contract to the applicant. If the insurance contract contains provisions on the exclusion of the insurer's liability, the insurer shall clearly explain such provisions to the applicant at the time of concluding the insurance contract; failure to clearly explain shall render such provisions null and void. Accordingly, the insurer has the obligation to clearly explain the liability exclusion clauses to the applicant when concluding the insurance contract. The aforementioned obligation is a statutory obligation and also a special duty of disclosure. If a dispute arises between the parties to the insurance contract as to whether the insurer has fulfilled this duty of disclosure, the insurer shall provide relevant evidence that it has given a clear explanation of the content of the relevant exclusion clauses; otherwise, such exclusion clauses shall not take effect.

Plaintiff: Duan Tianguo, male, 30 years old, Han Chinese, residing at Hengxi Street, Jiangning District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited, Nanjing Branch, domiciled at Longpan Road, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Person in charge: Lou Weimin, General Manager of the Branch.

The plaintiff, Duan Tianguo, filed a lawsuit with the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited, Nanjing Branch (hereinafter referred to as PICC Nanjing Branch), over a dispute concerning an insurance contract.

The plaintiff, Duan Tianguo, alleged: On March 24, 2008, the plaintiff entered into a third-party liability insurance contract with the defendant, PICC Nanjing Branch. On September 11, 2008, while driving the insured vehicle on the Longtong Line in the western section of Shucun Village, the plaintiff collided with a moped driven by a third party, Wang Dawei, resulting in a traffic accident causing damage to both vehicles and injury to Wang Dawei. The plaintiff demanded that the defendant pay the full insurance amount, but the defendant refused unreasonably. The plaintiff requested the court to order the defendant to pay insurance proceeds of RMB 72,825.68 to the plaintiff in accordance with the insurance contract.

The defendant, PICC Nanjing Branch, argued: 1. According to Article 9 of the terms of the insurance contract in question, even if a claim is settled, a 20% deductible should be applied. 2. According to Article 25, paragraph 2 of the terms of the insurance contract in question, the cost of non-medical insurance drugs amounting to RMB 4,080.20 for the injured person should not be covered.

The court of first instance, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, found the following facts:

On March 24, 2008, the plaintiff, Duan Tianguo, insured the tractor with license plate Su 0141557 with the defendant, PICC Nanjing Branch, under a motor vehicle third-party liability insurance policy with a coverage limit of RMB 200,000, for the period from March 25, 2008 to March 24, 2009. The parties specially agreed that the owner of the insured vehicle was Duan Tianling, and the insured was Duan Tianguo. Article 6, paragraph 7, item 2 of the insurance contract in question stipulated: "If the driver driving the insured vehicle does not hold a driving license corresponding to the type of vehicle indicated on the license, the insurer shall not be liable for any compensation for damage to third parties caused by any reason whatsoever." Article 9, item 1 stipulated: "On the basis of calculating the compensation amount in accordance with the terms of this insurance contract, within the liability limit specified in the insurance policy, the insurer shall apply a deductible according to the following rates... where the insured bears full responsibility for the accident, the deductible rate is 20%." Article 25, paragraph 2 stipulated: "The insurer shall determine the amount of medical expense compensation in accordance with the standards of the national basic medical insurance." The applicant's declaration section on the insurance application form stated: "The insurer has clearly explained the insurance clauses corresponding to the insurance types covered (including the liability exclusion part) to me, and I fully understand them. All the information filled in above is true, and I agree to use this application form as the basis for concluding the insurance contract." Duan Tianguo signed his name in the applicant's declaration column.

On September 11, 2008, the plaintiff, Duan Tianguo, drove the tractor Su 0141557 and collided with a two-wheeled moped driven by a third party, Wang Dawei, on the Longtong Line, resulting in damage to both vehicles and injury to Wang Dawei. The traffic police department determined that Duan Tianguo bore full responsibility for the accident. Wang Dawei subsequently filed a lawsuit in court. The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing rendered Civil Judgment No. (2009) Jiangning Min Yi Chu Zi No. 480 and Civil Ruling No. (2009) Jiangning Min Yi Chu Zi No. 480, ordering PICC Nanjing Branch to pay Wang Dawei RMB 111,075 within the liability limit of the compulsory traffic accident liability insurance separately purchased by Duan Tianguo, and ordering Duan Tianguo and Duan Tianling to jointly and severally pay Wang Dawei RMB 55,923.68. After the judgment took effect, Duan Tianguo requested PICC Nanjing Branch to settle the claim but was refused.

It was also found: The emergency medical expenses of RMB 2,402.30 for the third party, Wang Dawei, after the accident were not dealt with in Case No. (2009) Jiangning Min Yi Chu Zi No. 480. During the trial, the defendant, PICC Nanjing Branch, did not dispute the authenticity of the aforementioned emergency expenses. Therefore, the losses incurred by the plaintiff, Duan Tianguo, in this accident that were not compensated by the insurance company included: prepaid medical expenses of RMB 14,500, joint and several compensation of RMB 55,923.68, and emergency medical expenses of RMB 2,402.30, totaling RMB 72,825.98. At the time of the accident, the motor vehicle driving license held by Duan Tianguo was a Class B license issued by the traffic management department of the public security organ.

The above facts were confirmed by evidence including the insurance policy, the insurance application form, medical expense receipts, the motor vehicle driving license, the effective judgment and ruling, and the statements of the parties, and were sufficient to establish.

The focus of the dispute in this case was: Whether the defendant, PICC Nanjing Branch, should pay the insurance claim, and if so, how to determine the amount of the claim.

The court of first instance, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, held that:

The insurance contract concluded between the plaintiff, Duan Tianguo, and the defendant, PICC Nanjing Branch, represented the true intentions of both parties, was lawful and valid, and should be protected by law. When an accident occurs involving the insured vehicle, the insurance company shall compensate in accordance with the terms agreed upon by both parties in the insurance contract in question. This case occurred in 2008, and the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China as amended in 2002 (hereinafter referred to as the Insurance Law) shall apply.

Regarding whether the disputed clause of the insurance contract in question could be interpreted as "non-medical insurance drugs are not covered": Article 25, paragraph 2 of the insurance contract in question stipulated: "The insurer shall determine the amount of medical expense compensation in accordance with the standards of the national basic medical insurance." The plaintiff, Duan Tianguo, and the defendant, PICC Nanjing Branch, had different understandings of this provision. PICC Nanjing Branch argued that the meaning of this provision was that "non-medical insurance drugs" were not covered, while Duan Tianguo argued that the phrase "standards of the national basic medical insurance" in this clause had no specific or clear meaning, and PICC Nanjing Branch's definition of it as "the scope of medical drugs" lacked legal basis. In this regard, the court held that Article 41 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a dispute arises over the understanding of a standard clause, it shall be interpreted in accordance with the usual understanding. If there are two or more interpretations of a standard clause, the interpretation that is unfavorable to the party providing the standard clause shall prevail. If a standard clause is inconsistent with a non-standard clause, the non-standard clause shall prevail." Therefore, where the meaning of the disputed clause of the insurance contract in question was unclear, an interpretation unfavorable to PICC Nanjing Branch should be adopted.

Even if the disputed clause of the insurance contract in question could be understood as "non-medical insurance drugs are not covered", the validity of this clause should still be comprehensively analyzed in conjunction with the relevant legal provisions on insurance contracts. From the nature of an insurance contract, it is a contract of utmost good faith. The exclusion clauses of an insurance contract determine the risk of the applicant and the fundamental interests of the insurance, and have a decisive impact on whether the applicant decides to purchase the insurance. According to Article 17, paragraph 1, and Article 18 of the Insurance Law, "the insurer shall explain the terms and contents of the insurance contract to the applicant"; "if the insurance contract contains provisions on the exclusion of the insurer's liability, the insurer shall clearly explain such provisions to the applicant at the time of concluding the insurance contract; failure to clearly explain shall render such provisions null and void." Accordingly, when concluding an insurance contract, the insurer must clearly explain the liability exclusion clauses to the applicant. The aforementioned obligation is a statutory obligation and also a special duty of disclosure. This obligation not only requires that a professionally trained insurer qualified to engage in insurance matters draws the applicant's special attention to the exclusion clauses on the insurance policy, but, more importantly, requires a clear explanation of the content of the relevant exclusion clauses. If a dispute arises between the parties to the contract as to whether the insurer has clearly explained the exclusion clauses of the insurance contract, the insurer shall bear the burden of proof; that is, the insurer must also provide relevant evidence that it has given a clear explanation of the content of the relevant exclusion clauses; otherwise, such exclusion clauses shall not take effect. In this case, the evidence provided by PICC Nanjing Branch to prove that it had fulfilled its duty of disclosure was the applicant's declaration on the insurance application form and the signature of Duan Tianguo. However, the content of this declaration did not provide a clear explanation of the specific content of the disputed clause and could not prove that PICC Nanjing Branch had explained to Duan Tianguo that this clause contained the meaning of "non-medical insurance drugs are not covered", i.e., a partial exclusion of the insurer's liability. Therefore, even if this clause could be understood as "non-medical insurance drugs are not covered", it could not produce the corresponding legal effect.

Furthermore, the national basic medical insurance is a welfare-oriented social insurance system established to compensate workers for economic losses caused by the risk of illness. Its purpose is to establish a medical insurance fund through contributions from employers and individuals, and to provide certain financial compensation by the medical insurance agency for medical expenses incurred when insured persons seek medical treatment due to illness, so as to avoid or mitigate the economic risks faced by workers due to illness, treatment, etc. In order to control the expenditure on medical insurance drug costs, the national basic medical insurance limits the scope of drug usage. However, the insurance contract in question is a commercial insurance contract. The insurance premium charged by the insurer is far higher than that of the national basic medical insurance, and the insured's expectation of benefits from joining the insurance is also far higher than that of the national basic medical insurance. Therefore, if the disputed clause were interpreted according to the defendant, PICC Nanjing Branch's contention that "non-medical insurance drugs are not covered", it would significantly reduce the risk of PICC Nanjing Branch, reduce its obligations, and limit the rights of the plaintiff, Duan Tianguo. PICC Nanjing Branch collects premiums based on commercial insurance but settles claims according to the standards of national basic medical insurance, which is contrary to the principle of good faith.

In summary, the argument of the defendant, PICC Nanjing Branch, that "non-medical insurance drugs are not covered" based on the terms of the insurance contract in question was not upheld. The plaintiff, Duan Tianguo, did not purchase the "additional deductible waiver" insurance. The insurance clauses of the insurance contract in question clearly stipulated that the deductible rate for a driver bearing full responsibility for the accident was 20%. The opinion of PICC Nanjing Branch that a 20% deductible should be applied before settling the claim was consistent with the terms of the insurance contract in question and should be upheld.

Accordingly, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing rendered the following judgment on May 19, 2010:

The defendant, PICC Nanjing Branch, shall pay the plaintiff, Duan Tianguo, insurance proceeds in the amount of RMB 58,260.78.

After the judgment of first instance was announced, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory time limit, and the judgment of first instance has become legally effective.
